title: Shared HTTP/request helper family
problemStatement: API route modules were repeating small but correctness-critical request-handling logic: parseJsonBody error mapping, repo-resolution error mapping, and workspace invalid-request classification. That duplication had already caused real semantic drift where malformed client input returned 500 instead of 400/403/413/415.

duplicateClusters.name: Body parse classification drift
duplicateClusters.bestFix: Create one bounded helper for parseJsonBody error classification and response emission.

duplicateClusters.name: Repo resolution error mapping drift
duplicateClusters.bestFix: Create one bounded helper for repo-resolution 400/403 mapping and reuse it across route modules.

duplicateClusters.name: Workspace invalid-request classification drift
duplicateClusters.bestFix: Use one shared classifier for workspace allowlist and invalid-workspace request handling.

whyCurrentSharedModulesWereInsufficient: tools/api/response.js owned JSON response emission, but not request-classification policy.
Route modules had local helpers, but they were duplicated and could drift independently.
MCP and editor bridges use different transport/error envelopes, so the right fix was not a cross-protocol abstraction.

migrationsCompleted.notes: Now owns body-parse, repo-resolution, and workspace request classification helpers for HTTP routes.
Federated and search routes now use the shared helper family.

nonGoals: Unify HTTP, SSE, and MCP transport error envelopes in one abstraction.
Move validation or observability policy out of the route surfaces in this issue.
followOnDeletionTargets: Any remaining duplicated API request-classification branches that emerge after later route work.
